title: Integral ring maps induce algebraic residue-field extensions
statement: Let $\varphi:D\to E$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that every element of $E$ satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in $\varphi(D)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset E$ be a prime ideal and put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Write $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ for the residue fields of the corresponding affine-scheme points [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then the canonical field extension $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-pc-field-extension] is algebraic: every element of $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is a root of a nonzero polynomial over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. No injectivity, finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis on $\varphi$ is required.
